# Alternative Architecture: Serverless Full-Stack with a Managed Backend

**Generated by**: Claude Code (Lab 7, step 4)
**Date**: 2026-11-05
**Spec**: [specs/001-student-task-tracker/spec.md](../specs/001-student-task-tracker/spec.md)
**Compare with**: the base architecture in
[specs/001-student-task-tracker/plan.md](../specs/001-student-task-tracker/plan.md)

## Summary

Instead of running our own API server, worker and Redis, this alternative builds the app as a
single **Next.js** project deployed on **Vercel** and uses **Supabase** (managed PostgreSQL with
built-in authentication) as the backend. Security is enforced in the database with **Row-Level
Security (RLS)**. Reminders are sent by a **scheduled function** that runs every 5 minutes.
Nothing is a long-running server we have to operate.

## Architecture Overview

```text
 Browser
   │  HTTPS
   ▼
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ Next.js app on Vercel                    │
 │  • React pages (server + client rendered)│
 │  • Server Actions for writes             │
 │  • Cron route /api/cron/reminders (5 min)│
 └───────┬──────────────────────┬───────────┘
         │ Supabase client      │ (cron only, service key)
         ▼                      ▼
 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐      ┌──────────────┐
 │ Supabase                                 │      │ Resend email │
 │  • Auth (email + password, reset emails) │      │ API          │
 │  • PostgreSQL with Row-Level Security    │      └──────▲───────┘
 │  • SQL views: upcoming list, averages    │             │
 └──────────────────────────────────────────┘     cron sends reminders
```

## Components

| Component | Responsibility | Replaces in base architecture |
|-----------|----------------|-------------------------------|
| Next.js pages | UI, rendered on the server for fast first load | React SPA |
| Server Actions | Create/edit/delete courses and assignments | Express REST API |
| Supabase Auth | Sign up, sign in, password reset, sessions | Custom auth + session table |
| PostgreSQL + RLS | Data and per-student access rules (`student_id = auth.uid()`) | Query scoping in the service layer |
| SQL views/functions | Overdue flag, upcoming list, weighted course average | Service-layer logic |
| Vercel Cron | Every 5 minutes, finds reminders due now and sends them | Redis + BullMQ + worker |
| Resend | Transactional email API | SMTP provider via Nodemailer |

## How the requirements are met

| Requirement | How it's met |
|-------------|--------------|
| FR-001, FR-002 | Supabase Auth (email/password, built-in reset email) |
| FR-003 – FR-007 | Server Actions writing to Postgres tables; list filters are SQL queries |
| FR-008, FR-009 | `reminders` table with `send_at`; cron selects `pending` rows where `send_at <= now()`, re-checks the assignment is not done, sends, marks `sent`; up to 3 attempts |
| FR-010 | SQL view `course_averages` computes Σ(score×weight)/Σ(weight) |
| FR-011 | Calendar page queries assignments between week start and end |
| FR-012 | RLS policies on every table; even a bug in app code can't read another student's rows |
| FR-013 | Deleting the auth user cascades to all of the student's rows |

## Data model

The data model is the same as in the base plan's
[data-model.md](../specs/001-student-task-tracker/data-model.md), with these changes:
- `Student.id` is the Supabase `auth.users.id`; there's no `passwordHash` column (Supabase manages
  it).
- Every table has a `student_id` column so RLS policies are simple.
- `Reminder` gets an index on `(status, send_at)` for the cron query.

## Project structure

```text
app/                    # Next.js App Router pages: dashboard, courses, calendar, settings
  api/cron/reminders/   # Scheduled reminder route
lib/                    # Supabase client, server actions, grade helpers
supabase/
  migrations/           # Tables, RLS policies, views
tests/
  unit/                 # Vitest
  db/                   # pgTAP tests for RLS policies and views
  e2e/                  # Playwright
.github/workflows/ci.yml
```

## Deployment and operations

- **Hosting**: Vercel (app + cron) and Supabase (database + auth). Both have free tiers that cover
  a class project.
- **Environments**: Vercel preview deployment per pull request; a Supabase branch database per PR.
- **CI**: GitHub Actions runs lint, unit tests, database tests (Supabase CLI locally) and
  Playwright E2E tests before merge.
- **Monitoring**: Vercel and Supabase dashboards; failed reminders are visible as
  `status = failed` rows.

## Constitution Check

| Principle | Status | Notes |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| I. Simplicity | PASS | Fewer moving parts: no API server, worker or Redis to run |
| II. Spec-Driven | PASS | Built from the same spec.md |
| III. Test-First | PASS (with change) | No REST API to contract-test; contract tests target Server Actions and RLS policies instead |
| IV. Privacy & Security | PASS | RLS enforces data isolation in the database; Supabase hashes passwords |
| V. CI & Version Control | PASS | Same GitHub Actions workflow |

## Trade-offs compared with the base architecture

| Factor | Base (3-tier + worker) | Alternative (serverless + Supabase) |
|--------|------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| Time to first working version | Slower: we build auth, API and worker | Faster: auth and database come ready-made |
| Operations | We run 5 containers | No servers to manage |
| Cost at class-project scale | A small VM plus managed database and Redis | Usually free tier |
| Reminder timing | Exact (delayed jobs) | Up to 5 minutes late (still meets SC-003) |
| Vendor lock-in | Low: standard Docker, Postgres, SMTP | Medium: Supabase Auth/RLS and Vercel Cron are platform features |
| Public API for future mobile app | Yes: documented REST API | Weaker: Server Actions are web-only (Supabase's auto API could be used) |
| Testability | Clear REST contract tests | Needs database-level tests for RLS |
| Learning value for a team | Shows every layer explicitly | Hides auth and infrastructure behind services |

## Risks

- **Free-tier limits**: Supabase pauses free projects after a week of inactivity; Vercel Hobby
  cron frequency limits may require a paid plan or an external scheduler such as GitHub Actions.
- **RLS mistakes**: a missing policy can expose or hide data; this is mitigated by pgTAP tests for
  every table.
- **Cold starts**: serverless functions can add a few hundred milliseconds on the first request.
